headline.the_gap_is_closed_and_i_proved_the_check: The r7 arm, run through MY worktree with the DELIVERED tool, reports **2 collisions at 1920x1080 AND 2 at 1280x720** — `container.mine.head` 'Carried' x `container.mine.row.hist-bark-token` and `container.theirs.head` 'Reed Creel' x `container.theirs.row.bog-iron-maul`, intersection **190x20** at 1080p and **126.67x13.34** at 720p, with 2,482 / 1,873 ink px in the shared region. The delivered arm reports **0 at both**, `intersecting_pairs` 2 -> 0, `text_bearing` 17 on both arms. A tool that only ever goes green on the fix is the class of defect this round exists to close, and this one goes red on the defect.

headline.and_the_thing_the_round_could_not_settle: The builder reported SHEET RED on the OVERLAP leg at 1920x1080 and clean at 1280x720, level-up losing one of its two, and said plainly it had not established whether that was the screen or the instrument. **It is the instrument.** All SIX rows the leg reports have a label/value line that separates cleanly when the gauge bar is ablated out — `sheet.attr.willpower` goes from `separators 0` to `separators 2`, `levelup.attr.personality` from 1 to 7 — because the gauge fills **134 to 217 of the row's columns** and `rowProfile()` projects the WHOLE row rect down to one column profile. I cropped both screens at 4x and read them: 'WILLPOWER 10' and 'HIST-BOND 10' are set with clear space between label and value. **FD4's hard fail is NOT firing on these screens for a legibility reason, and 1280x720 is not safe either — both readings are noise about the gauge's tick spacing.**

job_4_the_pin_and_whether_it_is_fit_to_b.the_falsification_of_S65_2s_mechanism_is: S65(2) said to pin the D2 reference via `getUIState().materials`. `materials` is a list of names; the panel composites at CALM_ALPHA 0.94 over the world and `panel()` paints clay under a 0.55 slip, so the palette lookup is 0.90-4.64 dE00 from the real painted ground. My own run measures `palette_ground_dE00` at 1.896 (inventory, sheet), 2.238 (container), 2.872 (spells), **4.641 (level-up)**. The ruling's route does not exist and the builder was right to say so in the ruling rather than around it.
job_4_the_pin_and_whether_it_is_fit_to_b.MY_RULING_ON_THE_PIN: **THE PIN IS NOT FIT TO BE THE BAR AS WRITTEN, AND IT IS ALREADY WRITTEN INTO THE ITEM.** The builder declined to offer it as the bar or to claim anything on it (CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3 guard 2, correctly applied) — but it edited `RI-UIX09` method 4 to say 'the reference IS the shipped estimator over the panel's own declared ground probe'. A round cannot publish a method into the corpus and simultaneously decline to be judged by it; the next critic will read the item, not the status file.
job_4_the_pin_and_whether_it_is_fit_to_b.why_it_is_not_fit_yet_measured: The probe samples ground at ONE strip. On the container that is exact — `probe_vs_panelA_dE00` = 0.000 and the pinned figure equals the shipped one to four decimals, my own run. On the larger panels it is 1.577 (sheet) to 2.779 (level-up) dE00 away from the panel-rect reference, because 6% of every ground pixel is a world that varies across 1520x780 and one strip is not the whole ground. The consequence, my own numbers: **inventory 0.1550 -> 0.1439 and sheet 0.1594 -> 0.1490, i.e. two screens cross BELOW DN4's hard-fail floor purely by changing where the ground is sampled**, while level-up crosses the other way, 0.1509 -> 0.1579.
job_4_the_pin_and_whether_it_is_fit_to_b.AND_THE_GUARD_IT_SHIPPED_WITH_IS_NOT_A_G: The item's new text says a large `probe_vs_panelA_dE00` means the reading is `unresolved, not used`. **It names no threshold.** 2.779 either is or is not large and the item does not say, so the guard cannot fire and cannot fail — which is precisely the defect class this round was dispatched to close, arriving inside the fix for it. Filed as a corpus defect below with the number it needs.
job_4_the_pin_and_whether_it_is_fit_to_b.what_i_did_with_it: NOTHING IN THE PASSING DIRECTION, and nothing in the failing direction either. DN4 hard-fails under the shipped estimator (level-up unresolved at margin 0.0009 against band 0.0195) and hard-fails under the pin (inventory 0.1439 outright). **The cap does not depend on which reading you take, which is why I can state the pin's bias without it being the reason anything fails.**

the_finding_the_round_asked_for_and_coul.how_i_established_it: Ablation, not a story about a threshold (S63). `rowProfile()` projects an `attribute_row`'s WHOLE rect down to one column profile and counts runs of >= `gap` all-zero columns as separators; `separators < 2` is reported as an overlap. An attribute row's rect contains the label/value TEXT LINE and the horizontal GAUGE BAR beneath it. the_water_js_repair_that_is_not_T4s.verdict: INERT TO RENDERING, PROVEN MECHANICALLY, and the diagnosis is correct.
the_water_js_repair_that_is_not_T4s.the_break: F7 round 4 (17e6fc02) wrote comments containing backticks INSIDE `installWaterShader`'s JS template literal, terminating it at line 267. `window.__HARNESS` never appeared and every browser-driven tool on the branch was dead.
the_water_js_repair_that_is_not_T4s.how_i_checked_the_repair_is_inert: Two proofs. (1) `git show 2449637a -- game/src/render/water.js` changes 14 lines, 7 in and 7 out, and **0 of them fail the regex `^[+-][[:space:]]*//`** — every changed line is a whole-line comment, so no GLSL statement is touched. (2) Stronger: reduce every whole-line comment on BOTH versions to the bare token `//` and compare. `comment-stripped identical: true`, **0 differing lines**, 329 lines on both sides. The shader source the compiler sees after comment stripping is byte-identical. `node --check` passes on both my worktrees.
the_water_js_repair_that_is_not_T4s.why_this_check_and_not_a_screenshot: A comment inside a template literal IS part of the GLSL source string, so 'it is only a comment' is not automatically true — it is true here because the changed spans are entirely inside `//`-to-end-of-line runs, and that is what the second proof establishes rather than assumes.
the_water_js_repair_that_is_not_T4s.the_hazard_the_builder_names_is_right_an: A shader written as a JS template literal cannot contain a backtick anywhere including its comments, and this codebase's house style puts identifiers in backticks in every comment it writes. `node --check game/src/**/*.js` costs under a second. Nothing in `pre-commit` runs it.

bifurcation.note: === PASS 1, JUDGEMENT SIDE: FIDELITY === PROPERTIES: F18 layout integrity, M-F18.1/2/3. PERMITTED: our own captures at 1920x1080 and 1280x720, both arms, same crop box. FORBIDDEN: every Morrowind plate and every modern AAA screenshot. reference_items.why_not_ten: A screen below the item's own hard-fail floor cannot score above 2 by the item's stated aggregation. biggest_gap.what: `tools/ui/t4-r5-legibility.mjs`'s OVERLAP leg — the S58 legibility pass without which no density figure counts — reports 6 findings across level-up and the sheet that are not legibility defects. It projects an `attribute_row`'s whole rect down to one column profile and requires >= 2 runs of blank columns; the row rect contains a horizontal gauge bar that fills **134 to 217 of the row's 161-244 columns**, which destroys the separators no matter how the text is set. Ablated, every one of the 6 reported rows has a label/value line with 2 to 7 separators — `sheet.attr.willpower`, the worst, goes from `separators 0, runs 1` to `separators 2`. Read at 4x, 'WILLPOWER 10' and 'HIST-BOND 10' have wide clear space between label and value. The same blindness produces the opposite error at 1280x720, where the thinner gauge's antialiased ends open blank runs and the sheet is reported CLEAN for an equally irrelevant reason.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The next real legibility regression on the level-up or character screen — the two screens a player reads every time they spend souls — will be indistinguishable from the noise this leg is already emitting, exactly as round 4's regression was invisible to every instrument until the owner opened the game and could not read it. And in the other direction it is already costing: the round filed two 'pre-existing overlap findings' against `progress.js` and asked for a gap of their own, and a round dispatched at them would spend itself on a defect that is not there.

remedy.action: Make the OVERLAP leg measure the thing it is named for. Two changes, both small. (1) Profile the row's TEXT BAND, not the whole rect: take the sub-rect the label and value baselines actually occupy — derivable from the row's declared rect and the face metrics `drawText` uses, the same way `descLineCap()` already derives a line box — and run `rowProfile()` on that. (2) Give the leg a self-test in the shape the COLLISION leg already has: fixtures whose arms are REQUIRED to disagree, including (a) a round-4-style row with label, value and gauge printed on one another, which must be RED, (b) a clean row with a full-width gauge under separated text, which must be GREEN and which the current leg fails, and (c) the same clean row at 1280x720, which must give the SAME answer as (b). Assert the answer set has more than one member, exactly as the collision self-test does. Do NOT simply raise or scale `GAP` further — the threshold is not the defect; projecting a gauge and a text line onto one axis is.
remedy.acceptance: The repaired leg, run at 1920x1080 and 1280x720 at the delivered commit, reports **0 overlap findings on level-up and the sheet** while its new self-test's round-4-style fixture still comes back RED and the two viewports agree on every fixture. Proven in the direction rule 4 requires: the leg must be shown RED on an actual capture of a build whose attribute rows collide — round 4's arm is the positive control and `t4-r4-critic-overlap.mjs`'s own fixtures are the starting point — before it is trusted green. Then re-run the five-screen sweep and publish it; FD4's remaining hard-fail candidates at 1920x1080 must be zero or real.

secondary_observations.what: **S61's band was inherited, not measured.** The round scores `container_no_name` as crossing from unresolved to resolved by 0.0015 against a band of 0.0146 that was measured on r6/r7 geometry, on a screen whose every row rect this round moved. S61's own text: the band 'must be measured per screen and published with the score, by the same perturbation the critic used'. I score it unresolved and fail it closed, which costs the round nothing because DN4 caps the item anyway.

**The pin is in the corpus and the round declines to be judged by it.** `RI-UIX09` method 4 now reads 'the reference IS the shipped estimator over the panel's own declared ground probe'. Under it, inventory reads 0.1439 and sheet 0.1490 — below DN4's hard-fail floor, where the shipped reading passes them. The builder correctly refused to claim anything on an instrument it wrote (§1.3 guard 2) but wrote it into the item anyway, and the next critic will read the item. Either the pin is the method, in which case two more screens hard-fail DN4, or it is provisional and the item should say so.

**The pin's own guard names no number and therefore cannot fire.** The item says a large `probe_vs_panelA_dE00` makes the reading `unresolved, not used`. Measured on my own arm: container 0.000, sheet 1.577, inventory 1.821, level-up 2.779. Nothing in the item says which of those is large. A guard with no threshold is the same defect class as a check that cannot fail — inside the fix for one.

**The two arms differ in five RENDER files, not only in the UI.** `git diff --name-only a2ef1e5c HEAD -- game/src/` lists `render/actor.js`, `render/lib/lighting-recipes.js`, `render/renderer.js`, `render/sky.js`, `render/water.js` alongside the three UI files. **The item depictions are category shapes, not depictions of the item.** `shapeFor()` maps 45 carried records onto 19 shapes by category and name regex — a decent spread, not one fallback repeated.
